Wedding Invitation Website Checklist: What to Include

A wedding invitation website gives guests one place to revisit the details of the celebration. A clear layout helps people understand when to arrive, where to go and whom to contact—while the design can still reflect the couple’s story.

Start with the essential event details

Put the names of the couple, the wedding date and the main venue near the top of the page. Include the local time and time zone when guests may be travelling from another region. If the celebration has more than one event, distinguish the ceremony, reception and any related gatherings clearly.

Use consistent date formatting and write the venue name exactly as guests will see it on maps or signs. Avoid relying on a decorative image for important information; keep key details as readable text.

Add a simple schedule

List the main moments in chronological order. For example: guest arrival, ceremony, photographs, reception and dinner. You do not need to describe every minute. A concise schedule helps guests plan transport and understand whether they should arrive early.

If the schedule may change, add a visible “last updated” note and make sure the person responsible for the invitation can update the details before guests rely on them.

Make the venue easy to find

Include the full venue name, street address and a map link. Add a short note about parking, public transport or the closest landmark when it will help visitors. For destination weddings, include local travel guidance and accommodation suggestions only when the information is confirmed.

Test the map link on a phone. A guest who is already travelling should not have to search through a long paragraph to find the location.

Explain guest expectations clearly

If there is a dress code, describe it in plain language and explain any practical details. Mention accessibility arrangements, children’s attendance or other important expectations only when the couple has decided them. Keep the tone welcoming rather than overly formal.

If guests need to RSVP, provide the confirmed response method and deadline. Do not imply that a template has an RSVP form unless that feature is actually available in the selected design or connected service. A clear contact method can be a useful alternative.

Use photos and story elements with restraint

A short “our story” section can make an invitation feel personal. Choose a few photos that the couple is happy to share and write captions that add context. The purpose is to welcome guests into the celebration, not make them scroll through an entire photo archive before finding the venue.

Use the same visual style for headings, buttons and information cards. Keep contrast strong and text large enough to read on a small screen.

Review the page before sending it

  • Confirm names, date, time and time zone.
  • Check the venue address and map link.
  • Verify schedule and RSVP details with the couple.
  • Test the page on a phone and desktop.
  • Check that every important detail is available as selectable text.
  • Share the link with a small test group before sending it to all guests.

Frequently asked questions

What information should a wedding invitation website include?

At minimum, include the couple’s names, date, start time, venue and a contact method. A schedule, map, dress code, travel notes and RSVP instructions can make it more useful.

Can an online wedding invitation replace a printed invitation?

That depends on the couple and guest preferences. A website can make event details easy to update and revisit, while printed invitations may still be preferred for formal or keepsake purposes.

Should an RSVP form be included?

Include an RSVP form only if the chosen platform or template actually supports it. Otherwise, provide a clear response link or contact method and confirm the deadline.

Wishly features, templates and editor controls may change. Check the current product interface and the selected template for the latest options. Avoid sharing personal information that should remain private.
